n: The heading places David in the wilderness of Judah, a dry and desolate region. His physical thirst becomes a picture of his soul’s thirst for God. He seeks God eagerly, at the start of the day.

f.g: I seek you earnestly — the word is related to “dawn.”

n: He remembers seeing God’s power and glory in the sanctuary and longs to experience it again.

f.g: The holy place — the tabernacle where God’s presence dwelt.

n: God’s loyal love is better than life itself, so David will praise him. Relationship with God is worth more than survival.

f.w: thy lovingkindness is better than life

n: For the rest of his life, he will bless God and lift his hands in prayer.

f.g: The ancient posture of prayer and praise.

n: His soul is satisfied as if after a rich feast. Even in the desert, God feeds him.

f.g: The richest foods — a picture of complete satisfaction.

n: Lying awake at night, he thinks about God through the night watches.

f.g: The night was divided into watches (shifts) of guard duty.

n: God has been his help, so he sings for joy in the shelter of his wings.
His soul clings to God, and God’s right hand holds him up — a picture of mutual holding.

f.g: Clings to you, sticks close — the same word as “cleave” in Genesis 2:24.

n: Those who want to kill him will go down into the depths of the earth — the grave.

f.w: the lower parts of the earth
f.g: The underworld, the realm of the dead.

n: They will fall in battle and be left for scavengers.
The king will rejoice in God, and all who swear by God’s name will celebrate, while liars are silenced.

f.g: Takes oaths in God’s name — that is, is loyal to him.
